newsitem.title: USA: FDA panel recommends Roche weight loss drug.
newsitem.headline: FDA panel recommends Roche weight loss drug.

text.p: Hoffman-La Roche Inc, a unit of Switzerland's Roche Holding Ltd, said on Wednesday that a Food and Drug Administration advisory panel recommended the approval of its weight loss drug Xenical.
Xenical represents a new class of anti-obesity drugs called lipase inhibitors or fat blockers that prevents the absorption of fat by about 30 percent.
In its studies, Hoffmann-La Roche said three times as many patients on Xenical with a moderately reduced calorie diet lost 10 percent or more of body weight compared to a placebo with diet.
The average patient in the one-year clinical trials weighed 220 pounds and lost 20 pounds after taking Xenical and dieting, the company said.

Xenical-treated patients had statistically significant reductions in cholesterol and blood pressure and improvements in blood concentrations of glucose and insulin, compared with patients who only dieted and took a placebo, the company said.
Hoffmann-La Roche said the study was based on double-blind placebo-controlled and randomized studies involving more than 4,000 patients in the United States and Europe.
The patients took Xenical capsules three times a day and a moderately reduced calorie diet containing 30 percent fat, the company said.

Most common side effects reported were non-systemic and were primarily gastrointestinal, the company said. The effects were early in treatment and were self-limited and of short duration in most cases, the company said.
